titulo_es: The ipothetic period type I: what is possible

promosso.consejo: Particulum or adjective of school success.

bocciato.consejo: Particulum or adjective of school suspension.

passare.consejo: Regular verb of the first conjugation.

texto: In the condition with **se** the indicative present (or future) is used, and in consequence the present, future or imperative: **Se parti adesso, arriverai in tempo** (if you leave now, you will arrive on time); **Se hai tempo, chiama Anna** (if you have time, call Anna).
It expresses daily situations, general truths or direct instructions.
To deny, add **non**: **Se non piove, usciamo** (if it doesn't rain, we go out).
The consequence may be an order: **Se piove, chiudi la finestra**.

filas: If you go out now, you'll be there in time.
If you have time, call Anna.
If it rains, close the window

frases.it: Se passo un esame, sono contento.
frases.es: Si apruebo un examen, estoy contento.
frases.en: If I pass a test, I'm happy.

frases.es: Si tienes tiempo, llama a Anna.
frases.en: If you have time, call Anna.

frases.es: Si no llama, la vuelvo a llamar yo.
frases.en: If you don't call, I'll call you back.

bloques.pregunta: How is the hypothetical period of type I in Italian structured?

opciones.texto: «Se» + present indicative in condition, and present or future in consequence.
opciones.explicacion: It is the classic pattern for real or highly probable facts.
The conditional is never introduced directly after «se».

opciones.texto: «Se» + gerunde composed in both parts of the prayer.
opciones.explicacion: The gerunde does not introduce conditional prosecstasy with «se».
Informal second-person affirmative of the verb «aprire».
Close in Italian is expressed with «chiudi».
Cleaning would be expressed with «pulisci».

bloques.frase: Se hai tempo stasera, ___ ad Anna per confermare l'orario.

opciones.explicacion: Informal «chiamare» Imperative addressed to you.
It is the formal form of courtesy addressed to Lei («You call.»).
He is the first person in singular: «I'll call.».

opciones.texto: An imperative consequence conditioned by the weather of the rain.
opciones.explicacion: Type I hypothetical period with an apodosis imperative.

opciones.texto: It rained so much yesterday that it broke the glass from the window.
opciones.explicacion: It is an immediate present or future situation.

opciones.texto: That the speaker has the absolute certainty that it will not rain.
opciones.explicacion: It plans an open hypothesis: «if it rains».

bloques.pregunta: What causal relationship does this phrase establish?
bloques.frase: Se passo un esame, sono molto contento.

opciones.texto: It approves the review and as a direct consequence it is satisfied.
opciones.explicacion: Real condition with indicative present in both proposals.

opciones.texto: He usually stops the exams and gets angry with his teachers.
opciones.explicacion: «Passo un esame» means to approve, not to suspend.

opciones.texto: He studied during the summer but did not show up for the final test.
opciones.explicacion: Describe an emotional reaction to the approved one.

bloques.frase: Se studi con costanza impari molte cose nuove
bloques.traduccion: If you study with constancy you learn many new things
bloques.explicacion: The hypothetical period of reality with verbs in the present of indicative.

bloques.frase: Se studi con attenzione, ___ molti libri utili.

opciones.explicacion: Second person singular of this «leggere» indicative.
He is the first person in singular: «I read».
He is the first person to plural: «We read».

bloques.pregunta: What is the Italian term for a school exam?

opciones.explicacion: Adjective or particient that denotes not having passed the academic test.
«Promosso» means approved or promoted course.
«Laureato» appoints those who have obtained a university degree.

intro: Conditional phrases are organized in three types. We start with type I: it expresses real or very likely conditions in the present or future («If you study, you learn»).
